title: Evolve an async job queue in 3 steps: result tracking, status filter, and batch create
description: A minimal async FastAPI job queue (create/get/list) is evolved over three steps to become a production-ready queue API.

task_spec.prompt:
The async job queue API (src/app.py) has POST /jobs, GET /jobs/{id}, and GET /jobs. Evolve it in three steps:

Step 1 — Result tracking: Add an optional 'result' field (str | None, default None) to the job store. Add PATCH /jobs/{job_id}/status that accepts {"status": "<str>", "result": "<optional str>"} — updates both fields atomically. Return 404 if job not found. Update reset() to clear results too. Write test_update_status_with_result.

Step 2 — Status filter: Update GET /jobs to accept an optional ?status=<str> query param. When provided, return only jobs matching that status. When absent, return all. Write test_list_filter_by_status that creates two jobs, updates one, and asserts only matching jobs are returned.

Step 3 — Batch create: Add POST /jobs/batch that accepts a JSON array [{"name": ...}, ...] (max 10 items) and creates all jobs atomically. Return a list of created jobs with status 207 Multi-Status. Reject payloads exceeding 10 items with 422. Write test_batch_create and test_batch_create_too_many.

All existing tests must continue to pass. Run uv run pytest tests/ -v to confirm.
success_criteria: All three steps implemented in a single coherent module
followup_prompts: Good progress. Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to see where we stand. Continue with the remaining steps, prioritizing the parts the tests depend on most.
Final push: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and fix any remaining failures. Make sure the full implementation is complete and all tests pass.
